{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-30, revisiting at higher fidelity something he says he has raised several times.

HIS WORDS: *"creation of views must be native to domain of the design project."* Three cases he named — a 3D-printed component for a car engine (.stl or whatever the industry standard is for printing an alloy), his brother's garage (architectural blueprints in a format that domain accepts), and a self-sufficient biodome. And the question under all three: *"does the agent create the .stl file (not sure if it can or if it would be good) or does it guide the user through using blender or some other software"*.

⭐ HIS STATED FEAR IS THE CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS NOT GENERIC ANXIETY: *"an agent can be 'over confident' and can 'hallucinate' thereby giving a design artifact that can't be trusted or used or fills in design considerations without asking the designer."* Note the two halves — an artifact that is WRONG, and an artifact that QUIETLY DECIDES something the designer never chose. The second is the one reflow2 already has doctrine about.

DISTINCT FROM dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-project-that-is-not-software, which asks why the DELIVERY (skills, examples, defaults) is software-shaped when the vocabulary is neutral. This asks who holds the pen for the domain artifact itself, which is not among that node's five options.

═══ A REFRAMING WORTH TESTING BEFORE THE OPTIONS ═══

An .stl may be the wrong thing to argue about. It is triangle soup — a BUILD OUTPUT nobody reads or reviews, the CAD equivalent of a compiled binary. reflow2 has never claimed to write anybody's binary; it tracks the SOURCE that produces one, with a checksum, realizing a capability.

The reviewable source for a printed part is parametric: OpenSCAD, CadQuery, build123d. Text. Diffable. Checksummable. Deterministic to compile. A human can read it and disagree with it. If that is right, this case dissolves: the agent may author the SOURCE, because its errors are visible, and the .stl is a build artifact rather than a design artifact. UNTESTED, and it is the first thing to check rather than assert — it may not generalise past parts simple enough to be parametric.

═══ THE OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

(a) THE AGENT NEVER AUTHORS A DOMAIN ARTIFACT — it carries the design into the third-party tool and the result back. Safest against his fear, and it matches the division already stated for views (reflow2 serves content, the agent renders). Counter: it makes reflow2 a filing cabinet in domains where the artifact is cheap and reviewable, and an agent writing OpenSCAD is genuinely useful.

(b) THE AGENT AUTHORS ONLY WHAT A HUMAN CAN REVIEW — parametric source, schedules, bills of material, specifications; never opaque geometry, never analysis results. THE LINE IS NOT THE FORMAT, IT IS REVIEWABILITY. Counter: reviewability is a judgement and will be argued at every boundary.

(c) A THIRD TIER THE OTHER TWO MISS — artifacts the agent must not author for LEGAL rather than quality reasons. A garage needs a permit, and in most jurisdictions a structural drawing is stamped by a licensed engineer. An FEA result for an engine component under thermal and cyclic load is a professional judgement somebody is accountable for. Not a hallucination risk; a licensure boundary, and no amount of agent competence crosses it.

(d) REFLOW2 OWNS ONE CLASS NATIVELY, WHATEVER THE DOMAIN — the systems-engineering artifacts: requirements, interfaces, allocations, verification matrices, and resource/mass/energy balances. Domain-neutral by construction, and what reflow2 already IS. On the biodome that may be the most valuable artifact and nobody else produces it: `Flow`, `Resource` and budget `Constraint` already carry roughly a mass-and-energy balance, and the SV-7 measures/budgets viewpoint already renders one.

(e) THE DOCTRINE ALREADY EXISTS AND ONLY NEEDS EXTENDING. docs/viewpoints.md: *"If rendering requires extrapolating or filling in missing details, that is a sign something is missing or wrong inside reflow2 — not a prompt to improvise."* `cap:no-fabricated-repair` says the same for repairs. Extended to domain artifacts: IF PRODUCING THE ARTIFACT REQUIRES DECIDING SOMETHING NOBODY STATED, THAT IS A GAP TO ASK ABOUT, NOT A BLANK TO FILL. This answers the second half of his fear — the quiet fill-in — with machinery that already exists. It does NOT answer the first half: a confident wrong number nobody asked about is still wrong.

═══ WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED ═══
Whether an agent can produce a USABLE parametric part for a real mechanical requirement has not been tried here. Every option above reasons about capability rather than showing evidence of it, and Anthony's own standing question — what did you actually measure — applies to this node as much as to anything else.","name":"OPEN — when the design's artifacts are an .stl, a blueprint or a mass balance, does the agent AUTHOR them or carry the design into the tool that does?","rationale":"Captured under the brainstorm skill. Recorded as an open question because the artifact-authorship boundary is genuinely unsettled and the answer differs by domain and by legal exposure — writing it as a requirement would assert a policy nobody has chosen. The reframing (an .stl is a build output; parametric source is the design artifact) is offered as the cheapest thing to test first, not as the answer.
